system.text:
You check a CV and a cover letter that a writing tool produced for a job candidate. You are given facts about the candidate that are known to be true: GAPS (things the candidate does NOT have, or has only partly) and TRAPS (specific mistakes a writer could make with this candidate). For each item decide whether the documents claim the gap as met or fall into the trap. Each document is the text of the PDF the employer receives.

Rules:
- Judge only the two documents below. Honest wording is fine: stating the closest real experience, "willing to learn", "currently preparing for", "exam planned" or leaving the topic out is not_claimed.
- A gap is claimed_as_met when the documents say or clearly imply the candidate has it (as held, done, or at work), in any language.
- A trap is claimed_as_met when the documents make that mistake.
- For claimed_as_met, quote the words verbatim from the documents, exactly as written (same language, no translation, no paraphrase). Never invent a quote. If you cannot quote it, answer unclear.
- Answer every item id exactly once.

# GAPS (the candidate does not have these)

# OUTPUT 2: COVER LETTER
MARTA KOWAL-BRANDT
marta.kowalbrandt@example.com | +48 555 303 303 | gitlab.com/mkb-example
Corvale Mobility
Application: Cloud Infrastructure / DevOps Contractor - Fleet Connectivity
Dear Hiring Team,
I am applying for the Cloud Infrastructure / DevOps Contractor role in Fleet Connectivity. I
bring hands-on ownership of CI/CD pipelines and containerised test environments supporting
3 product teams and approximately 25 developers. With 7 years in QA automation and the
last two focused mainly on pipelines, environments and build tooling, I am seeking to move
into DevOps / platform engineering full time. Your scope of supporting backend developers
and building infrastructure from the outset aligns with that direction.
At Odrava Health Software, I own GitLab CI pipelines covering builds, unit, integration and
end-to-end tests, and artifact publishing. I reduced average pipeline time from 38 to 14
minutes through parallel test execution, dependency caching and on-demand ephemeral
environments. I also built per-merge-request environments using Docker Compose and
subsequently Helm charts on the company’s shared Kubernetes cluster. This experience
provides a practical foundation for supporting developers with repeatable environments and
faster feedback.
My work also combines automation with analytical troubleshooting. I maintain approximately
900 pytest and Playwright tests and reduced their flaky test rate from 7% to under 1%. I
write Bash and Python tooling for PostgreSQL test data seeding, use Linux, and have
experience with Grafana dashboards for test metrics. Earlier, I investigated customer issues
through logs and databases and reproduced bugs for developers. These experiences are
relevant to your emphasis on observability, reliability and clear collaboration between
infrastructure and backend teams.
Corvale’s fleet-connectivity platform has a broader scope than my current test-infrastructure
work, including telemetry ingestion, alerting and remote content updates. I would welcome a
conversation about how my CI/CD ownership, environment automation and troubleshooting
experience could contribute to the team as I make this transition into DevOps.
Kind regards,
Marta Kowal-Brandt

id.description: The item id as given (G1, G2, ... for gaps, T1, T2, ... for traps)

verdict.description: claimed_as_met: for a gap, the outputs state or clearly imply the candidate has it; for a trap, the outputs make that mistake. not_claimed: they do not. unclear: you cannot tell

document.description: Where the quote is from; none if not claimed

quote.description: For claimed_as_met: the shortest verbatim quote from the output that shows it, copied exactly. Empty otherwise

items.description: One entry per given item, every id exactly once
